1.title: Azure Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Azure Storage. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Compare Azure Storage services. Describe storage tiers. Describe redundancy options. Describe storage account options and storage types. Identify options for moving files, including Az Copy, Azure Storage Explorer, and Azure File Sync. Describe migration options, including Azure Migrate and Azure Data Box. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Storage accounts and the storage services
1.text: Storage accounts and the storage services. An Azure storage account is a container that holds your storage services under one globally unique name (three to twenty-four lowercase letters and numbers). Data is encrypted at rest by default and is reached over H T T P S. Azure Blob Storage. What it stores: Unstructured data (objects): documents, images, video, backups, logs. Use it for: Large amounts of files; serving content; backups; data lakes. Azure Files. What it stores: Fully managed file shares (S M B and N F S (Network File System)). Use it for: Replace or extend on-premises file servers; shared drives; lift and shift.

1.title: Storage accounts and the storage services, continued
1.text: Storage accounts and the storage services. Azure Queue Storage. What it stores: Messages in a queue. Use it for: Pass messages between app components, asynchronous work. Azure Table Storage. What it stores: No sequel key-attribute data (structured, no schema). Use it for: Flexible datasets such as user data or device information. Azure Disk Storage (managed disks). What it stores: Disks for virtual machines. Use it for: O S and data disks for V Ms. Exam tip: Match the data type: files to Blob (objects) or Files (shares); messages to Queue; structured No sequel to Table; V M disks to Disk. A "file share mapped like a network drive" to Azure Files.

1.title: Storage access tiers (Blob Storage)
1.text: Storage access tiers (Blob Storage). Tiers trade storage cost against access cost and speed. You choose a tier by how often you read the data. Hot. Access: Frequent. Storage cost: Highest. Access cost: Lowest. Minimum stay: None. Notes: Online, active data. Cool. Access: Infrequent. Storage cost: Lower. Access cost: Higher. Minimum stay: thirty days. Notes: Online, short-term backups. Cold. Access: Rare. Storage cost: Lower still. Access cost: Higher still. Minimum stay: ninety days. Notes: Online. Archive. Access: Almost never. Storage cost: Lowest. Access cost: Highest. Minimum stay: one hundred eighty days. Notes: Offline: data must be rehydrated (takes hours) before it can be read.

1.title: Storage access tiers (Blob Storage), continued
1.text: Storage access tiers (Blob Storage). for minimum periods and prices. The Archive tier can only be set per blob, and data in Archive cannot be read directly. Exam tip: "Data accessed rarely, lowest storage cost, can wait hours to read" to Archive. "Frequently accessed" to Hot. The cheaper the storage, the more it costs to read.

1.title: Redundancy options
1.text: Redundancy options. Azure keeps multiple copies of your data to protect against failures. You choose how far apart they are. L R S (locally redundant storage) (locally redundant). Copies: three. Where: One datacenter in one region. Protects from: Server rack or drive failure. Z R S (zone-redundant storage) (zone-redundant). Copies: three. Where: Three or more availability zones in one region. Protects from: A datacenter (zone) failure. G R S (geo-redundant storage) (geo-redundant). Copies: six. Where: L R S in the primary region, plus L R S in a paired secondary region. Protects from: A regional disaster.

1.title: Redundancy options, continued
1.text: Redundancy options. G Z R S (geo-zone-redundant storage) (geo-zone-redundant). Copies: six. Where: Z R S in the primary region, plus L R S in a secondary region. Protects from: Zone failure and regional disaster. R A G R S or R A G Z R S. Copies: six. Where: Same as G R S or G Z R S, plus read access to the secondary. Protects from: Regional disaster, with reads from the secondary.

1.title: Redundancy options, continued
1.text: Redundancy options. The figure shows this: Storage redundancy: L R S, Z R S, G R S and G Z R S.

1.title: Redundancy options, continued
1.text: Redundancy options. Local and zone options keep data in one region; geo options also copy it to a paired region. The secondary of G R S or G Z R S is not readable unless you choose the read-access (R A) variant, or a failover happens. Exam tip: Cheapest equals L R S. Datacenter failure equals Z R S. Regional disaster equals G R S or G Z R S. Read from the secondary equals R A-. Copies in a different region always mean a geo option.

1.title: Storage account options
1.text: Storage account options. Performance. Standard (hard disk, general purpose) or Premium (solid state, low latency). Account types. General-purpose version two (the standard type for most scenarios: blobs, files, queues, tables); Premium accounts for block blobs, file shares or page blobs, for high-performance needs. Redundancy. L R S, Z R S, G R S, G Z R S, and the read-access variants. Access tier (default). Hot or Cool. Use Premium when the workload needs consistently low latency and high transaction rates.

1.title: Moving files to and within Azure
1.text: Moving files to and within Azure. Az Copy. What it does: A command-line tool to copy blobs and files to or from a storage account. Notes: Good for scripts and large copies. Azure Storage Explorer. What it does: A graphical application to browse and manage storage accounts (blobs, files, queues, tables). Notes: Runs on Windows, mac O S and Linux.

1.title: Moving files to and within Azure, continued
1.text: Moving files to and within Azure. Azure File Sync. What it does: Syncs on-premises Windows file servers with Azure Files and caches frequently used files locally. Notes: Keeps the on-premises server as a fast cache while data lives in Azure.

2.title: Migration options
2.text: Migration options. Azure Migrate. A central hub of tools to discover, assess and migrate on-premises servers, databases, web apps and virtual desktops to Azure. Azure Data Box. A physical, ruggedized device Microsoft ships to you: you load data offline and send it back to be uploaded to Azure. Used for large amounts of data or slow networks (Data Box Disk, Data Box, Data Box Heavy). Exam tip: Servers and apps to Azure Migrate. Terabytes of data with limited bandwidth to Azure Data Box. Keep a local file server cache to Azure File Sync. Copy with a command to Az Copy. Click-and-browse tool to Storage Explorer.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors needs a shared network drive in Azure that on-premises servers can map using S M B (Server Message Block). Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Files. Azure Files provides managed file shares using S M B (and N F S). Blob stores unstructured objects.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Data must be kept for years, is almost never read, and the lowest storage cost matters more than read speed. Which tier fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Archive. Archive has the lowest storage cost; data is offline and must be rehydrated, which takes hours.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A company needs its data copied to another region so it survives a regional disaster. Which redundancy option provides this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: G R S. G R S (or G Z R S) copies data to a secondary region. L R S and Z R S stay in one region.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A company must move two hundred T B to Azure over a slow network. What is the best option? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Data Box. Data Box transports large data volumes offline on a physical device.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Which tool synchronizes an on-premises Windows file server with Azure Files? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure File Sync. Azure File Sync keeps file servers and Azure Files in sync with local caching.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Which storage service holds messages that application components pass to each other? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Queue Storage. Queue Storage stores messages for asynchronous communication.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which redundancy option protects against the loss of a single datacenter by spreading copies across availability zones? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Z R S. Z R S keeps three copies in three zones of one region.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which storage service is for unstructured objects? Answer: Azure Blob Storage. Question two. Name the four blob tiers. Answer: Hot, Cool, Cold and Archive. Question three. Which tier is offline and needs rehydration? Answer: Archive.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many copies do L R S and Z R S keep? Answer: Three copies each (L R S in one datacenter, Z R S across three zones). Question five. What does the R A prefix add to G R S? Answer: Read access to the secondary region. Question six. Az Copy or Storage Explorer: which is command line? Answer: Az Copy.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Which service discovers and assesses on-premises servers for migration? Answer: Azure Migrate.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Services: Blob equals objects; Files equals S M B or N F S shares; Queue equals messages; Table equals No sequel; Disk equals V M disks. Tiers: Hot (frequent) to Cool (thirty days) to Cold (ninety days) to Archive (one hundred eighty days, offline, rehydrate). Redundancy: L R S three copies one datacenter; Z R S three zones; G R S or G Z R S add a paired region. Account: standard general-purpose version two for most; premium for low latency; globally unique name. Move files: Az Copy (command line); Storage Explorer (gooey); File Sync (on-premises file server cache). Migrate: Azure Migrate (servers, databases, apps); Data Box (offline, huge data). In the next module, we continue the course.
